Marketing Campaign Brief

PLG\_Campaign Optimizer – 2026

| Prepared by: | Jessica Vose |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Date:** | June 25, 2026 |
| **Campaign:** | Campaign Optimizer PLG |

This document outlines a PLG launch campaign designed to drive self-serve trial signups among AdOps and campaign management teams at mid-size publishers. The campaign leads with a real, quantifiable problem — unmonitored campaign delivery leaking revenue — and converts through a frictionless free trial of Kana Campaign Management.

| Campaign: *PLG\_Campaign Optimizer* |
| :---- |

| WHY |
| :---- |

| Campaign Synopsis | A product-led growth campaign targeting AdOps managers, campaign managers, and ad operations teams at mid-size publishers (Time, Forbes, Condé Nast verticals, Hearst, Penske Media, Dotdash Meredith, etc.) who are manually monitoring campaigns in Google Ad Manager and consistently missing delivery failures until after the damage is done. The campaign leads with the revenue cost of under-delivery and broken creatives — the "silent tax" — and converts through a frictionless 14-day free trial that surfaces a real delivery risk in the prospect's own GAM account within minutes of signup. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Business Goal** | Generate 150 qualified free trial signups from AdOps and campaign management teams at mid-size publishers within 90 days of launch Drive trial-to-paid conversion at ≥ 20%, targeting $10K MRR from campaign-sourced customers by Day 90 Build brand awareness and SEO authority in the publisher ad operations category Establish Kana as the go-to real-time monitoring and optimization layer for Google Ad Manager users Create pipeline for Growth and Scale tier upgrades from trial users |

| WHO |
| :---- |

| Target Audience | Target companies: Time, Forbes, Condé Nast (mid-tier titles), Hearst Digital, Dotdash Meredith mid-market, Penske Media Corporation, Arena Group, Recurrent Ventures, Bustle Digital Group, Future plc US properties, Vox Media (mid-tier), Bauer Media, regional media groups with digital ad operations teams. Primary (hands-on operators): Ad Operations Manager / Senior Ad Operations Manager Campaign Manager / Senior Campaign Manager Ad Operations Specialist / Coordinator Ad Trafficker / Senior Ad Trafficker Programmatic Campaign Manager Yield Manager / Inventory Manager Ad Operations Analyst Ad Technology Manager Secondary (economic buyers): Director of Ad Operations VP of Ad Operations Head of Digital Revenue / Digital Advertising Revenue Operations Director Director of Digital Partnerships SVP/VP of Digital Media |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Persona** | An Ad Ops Manager or Campaign Manager at a mid-size digital publisher (50–500 person company, $10M–$200M revenue) who is manually monitoring hundreds of GAM line items each morning, struggling to catch under-delivery and pacing issues before they become costly refunds. They want real-time visibility without adding to their workload. They discover tools through AdMonsters, LinkedIn, and peer recommendations. Their director or VP cares about makegood rates, margin, and advertiser retention — and needs something they can show ROI on fast. |
| **Pain Points** | Manually monitoring thousands of GAM line items in spreadsheets — missing critical errors until budgets are wasted (79% of publisher ad ops teams still rely on manual processes) Under-delivery detected too late, after campaigns miss goals and makegoods are owed Broken creatives running for days before anyone notices, burning spend and damaging advertiser relationships Revenue leakage from GAM misconfigurations: research shows 10–25% of yield can drain without a trace from targeting conflicts, frequency cap errors, and consent issues Fragmented tech stacks with no unified view of campaign health — 55% of ad ops teams cite disconnected systems as a key barrier to scaling Reactive firefighting every morning instead of proactive optimization GAM reports delivery status but doesn't explain why campaigns are at risk or what to do about it Pacing errors compounding across hundreds of campaigns, creating cumulative revenue loss |

| WHAT |
| :---- |

| Key Message | Kana sees what GAM misses and fixes it before you lose the revenue. |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Supporting Messages** | 1\. "Stop monitoring campaigns manually. Kana monitors every line item in real time so your team doesn't have to." (Proof: teams spend 4–6 hours/week on manual GAM checks; Kana automates this entirely) 2\. "Catch delivery problems before they become refunds. Kana forecasts under-delivery risk before campaigns miss goals — not after." (Proof: direct-sold under-delivery can drain $2K–$5K+ per month per issue when caught late) 3\. "Get the real story behind campaign performance. Kana explains why something is going wrong — not just that it is." (Proof: GAM reports delivery status; Kana surfaces root cause and recommended action via conversational AI) 4\. "Deploy in minutes. No rip-and-replace." (Proof: Kana connects directly to your existing GAM stack — no custom builds, no IT tickets) |
| **Content Format** | Multi-format content engine: **WHITE PAPER** — "The Silent Tax: How Unmonitored Campaign Delivery Is Costing Mid-Size Publishers Millions" Top-of-funnel demand generation and credibility building. Gated for lead capture; ungated excerpt drives SEO.  Targets Directors and VPs who need board-level ammunition.  Covers: the state of publisher ad ops in 2026, the five most expensive delivery failures in GAM, the math on revenue leakage at 250M/500M/1B impressions/month, a buyer's guide checklist for evaluating monitoring solutions, and 2026 AdOps benchmarks. Production: 3–4 weeks. **BLOG POSTS —** "5 Campaign Delivery Issues GAM Won't Alert You To (Until It's Too Late)" SEO-targeted content capturing AdOps practitioners searching for GAM troubleshooting and pacing solutions.  Covers: creative errors that bypass GAM alerts, under-pacing masked until the final week, frequency cap misconfigurations, targeting conflicts suppressing delivery, and programmatic eCPM drops hidden in averages. CTA: 14-day free trial.  Target keywords: "Google Ad Manager under-delivery," "GAM campaign pacing issues," "ad ops campaign monitoring." Production: 5–7 business days. **Customer spotlight content:** Highlight real questions that emerged in customer conversations and how they were explored |
| **Key Action** | Visit kana.ai, select a pricing tier that works for you, and enter your credit card, connect to GAM. |

| ✨ Additional Content & Channel Recommendations |
| :---- |

Builds credibility and deepens the partnership narrative. **Research report:** After 6+ months, compile findings, community insights, and customer stories into an annual “State of What’s Possible” report – a gated asset for lead generation. **“Can AI…?”** challenge: For use at events. Come and submit your “What if AI could…” idea to us, we’ll review and select the best one. The best idea gets… **FAQ fuel:** Use the content generated and submitted for our FAQs on the website  **Additional Channels to Consider:** **YouTube:** Host longer-form “Can AI…?” explorations and demos, which also support SEO and can be embedded in blog posts. **Partner co-marketing:** Collaborate with complementary martech companies to co-produce “Can AI…?” content, expanding reach to their audiences. **Paid social amplification:** After identifying top-performing organic posts, invest in LinkedIn Sponsored Content and X/Twitter promoted posts to extend reach to lookalike audiences. **Industry events and webinars:** Pitch a “Can AI…?” workshop or panel at marketing conferences. Interactive format differentiates from typical vendor presentations. **Community platforms:** Seed questions and content in marketing communities like MarketingOps, CMO Coffee Talk, Pavilion, and relevant Slack groups. **Email signature link:** Include a rotating “This week’s Can AI question” in Kana team email signatures to drive passive traffic. |
